why: D5. A `companion object`'s members fold onto the enclosing type: `make()` is `java:shop.make.Widget.make`, not `…Widget.Companion.make`. The justification is what call sites actually write — `Widget.make()` from outside and a bare `make()` from inside both name the class, and nothing anywhere writes `Companion`, so a separate node would be a name the graph invented rather than read. The fixture exercises **all three** call forms — `Widget.make()` from outside, a bare `make()` from inside, and the explicit `Companion.make()` — so all three have to land on the same id, and it includes a `const val` in the companion because constants fold the same way. §6 assigned three forms to this case and the fixture long carried only two; the missing one is the form most likely to mint the very phantom D5 exists to prevent, because `Companion` is a bare capitalised name that no file declares. `Widget()` inside `make()` is the constructor case: instantiation is a call to the Type.

refusals.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `Companion` is a capitalised bare name that no file declares, so the ordinary `Type.member()` path resolves it under the enclosing package and produces `java:shop.make.Companion.make` — a class the source never mentions, carrying the member D5 says belongs to `Widget`. This is the fabrication D5 exists to prevent, and it is the reason this call form belongs in the fixture rather than only in the prose.
